visible.why: noon at a coffee cart: Spud holds out three coins; a rich lady slaps a $10,000,000 check on the counter
close: both stare down at the check, mouths open, his coins fall
low angle: the Duchess points up at the noon sun; Spud and Chip look up with her
he pushes a stack of notes into the seller's hands and grabs the cart's handle: he bought the whole cart; Chip jumps for joy
he sips his coffee in front of a mountain of money bags taller than the shops; one bag is gone from the top
a showroom: he slams a money bag on the gold car, the seller hands him the keys; outside the window Chip points at a green hill
a boutique: Spud in a fur coat admires himself in a gold mirror; Chip tugs his sleeve; he waves him off
in front of a white mansion he signs the deed on the agent's clipboard; behind him Chip's raised arm drops, his smile fades
late afternoon: Chip walks away alone up a path toward the cliff hill, looks back once
evening of day 6: alone in the gold car, the seat beside him piled with boxes where Chip sat; his face empty
day 6, a harbour: Spud signs for a yacht at the Duchess's stand and throws his arms up
the white yacht he just bought, side-on in full at sunset; then his private jet roars low over it
the gold coupe races along the coast road at sunset
from the car: up on the green cliff sits Chip alone against the sunset
close in the car: his eyes on the hill, he pulls the handbrake
the coupe at the roadside, its door open, the fur coat and gold chain left on the seat; Spud walks away up the slope in his sweater
a tow truck hooks the gold car and drives off; Spud climbs on and never looks back
the cliff top: Spud sits down beside Chip; Chip grins
from behind: the two friends small on the cliff, a huge sunset over the sea
close: Spud smiles for the first time; Chip leans his head on him
the last sliver of the sun, the first star
